items.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: if a martian came down to earth and listened to say Dizzy Gillespie, and say listened to Pete Candoli

ctx.x: Yeah. Well Louis Armstrong seemed to have the same — up until Parker he was kind of I guess the man who set the standard and most people were compared to him, especially the trumpet players, would be compared with him.

Yeah, right. And you know the differences that manifest itself in a particular person, has to be heard in the public consciousness long enough for the difference to be solidified in other people’s minds. You know what I mean? For them to say oh, this is a different style, this is Roy Eldridge. You know what I mean? Whatever that difference is, it has to be heard often enough by enough people, musicians, whatever, to be able to discern the little bit of difference. Because no two people are exactly alike. And the…
Can I ask you about the film “Bird,” how that came about? You played some on the soundtrack.
